title: zero-dimensional-etale-cohomology-rest
statement:
Let u be a universe, k : Type u an algebraically closed field, C : Scheme.{u}, and f : C ⟶ Spec k a separated, locally finite-type, quasi-compact morphism. Assume topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 0. Let F be a sheaf of abelian groups in universe u+1 on the small étale site of C. For each underlying point x : C choose an algebraically closed field Ω(x) : Type u and a morphism s(x) : Spec Ω(x) ⟶ C whose unique source point maps to x. No algebraicity of Ω(x) over k or extra linearity condition on s(x) is assumed. Then (1) for every natural number q > 0 the abelian group H^q(C,F), computed by Etale.cohomology applied to F placed in degree zero by DerivedCategory.singleFunctor, is subsingleton; and (2) the canonical morphism from H^0(C,F) to the categorical product over x : C of the geometric stalks F_{s(x)} is an isomorphism. This morphism is precisely the composite of homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso.hom, rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf.hom.app F, restriction F.ΓRes to the identity étale object C ⟶ C, and Pi.lift of the toPresheafFiber germs at s(x). The cohomology, site, abelian sheaves and geometric stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Finiteness is not an added hypothesis or a conjunct of this statement.

theorem zero_dimensional_etale_cohomology_rest (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 0) (F : Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (Ω : C → Type u) [∀ x, Field (Ω x)] [∀ x, IsAlgClosed (Ω x)] (s : ∀ x : C, Spec (.of (Ω x)) ⟶ C) (hs : ∀ x : C, (s x).base.hom default = x) : (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → Subsingleton ((Etale.cohomology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} C q).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) 0).obj F))) ∧ IsIso ((Functor.homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso (Sheaf.Γ C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) F 0).hom ≫ (Functor.rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf (Sheaf.Γ C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).hom.app F ≫ F.ΓRes (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 C))) ≫ Pi.lift (fun x : C => (Scheme.pointSmallEtale (s x)).toPresheafFiber (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 C)) (Over.homMk (s x) (Category.comp_id (s x))) F.obj))

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian], the finite-type
zero-dimensional scheme $C$ has finite discrete underlying space and every
point is closed. Let $i:C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ be the reduction. By
[lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced
and $i$ is a universal homeomorphism. Since $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a closed
subscheme of the finite-type $k$-scheme $C$, it is itself finite type over $k$.
Applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] to $C_{\mathrm{red}}$
identifies every residue field $\kappa_{C_{\mathrm{red}}}(c)$ with $k$ (equivalently,
$\mathcal O_{C_{\mathrm{red}},c}=\mathcal O_{C,c}/\sqrt{0}$ has the same
residue field). The singleton pieces of the finite discrete space
$C_{\mathrm{red}}$ are open and closed. Each such piece is affine by
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine]. Its coordinate ring is reduced
and has only one prime, hence is a field; the residue-field identification
makes that field $k$. Therefore each piece is $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the morphism from the coproduct of
these pieces to $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ induced by their inclusions is an
isomorphism: its restriction to each summand is the corresponding open
immersion, and the summands are pairwise disjoint and cover $C_{\mathrm{red}}$,
so it is bijective and a local isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-geometric-point-coproduct-cohomology] to the finite coproduct obtained in step 1 and the restriction of F. Positive cohomology is zero and the degree-zero canonical product-of-germs morphism is invertible. The chosen geometric points s(x) factor uniquely through the reduction, since Spec Ω(x) is reduced. On each Spec k summand, arbitrary algebraically closed geometric fields give the same exact stalk evaluation functor by Stacks Theorem 03QT and Lemma 03QU (the absolute Galois group of k is trivial); this extends the coproduct calculation stated for the canonical k-points to the specified s(x). No assumption that Ω(x) is algebraic over k is needed.

source.place: Theorem 03QT, Lemma 03QU, Section 03QQ; Lemma 0A5B, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Use [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] for i : C_red → C from [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] to transport all cohomology groups of the inverse image of F to those of F. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] to i and the lift of each specified s(x). Its germ formula identifies the product of pulled-back germs with the product of germs at s(x), after the unit comparison and the point bijection. Naturality of the degree-zero derived-to-underived comparison and restriction to the terminal étale object therefore identifies the transported isomorphism with exactly the displayed Lean composite. Positive-degree zero abelian groups have subsingleton underlying types. This proves the two conjuncts without assuming finiteness or reducedness of C.
